title: 頃（ころ／ごろ）— “around (a time) / when ～”
summary: 頃 marks an approximate time. It is read ごろ after a specific time (三時ごろ) and ころ after a period or event (子どものころ). It expresses “around ～” or “back when ～.”

patterns.gloss: 三時ごろ / 十月ごろ / 昨日ごろ

patterns.form: 名詞・動詞の普通形 ＋ ころ
patterns.gloss: 子どものころ / 高校のころ / 若かったころ

body.p: The same kanji 頃 is read ごろ (voiced) after a point in time and ころ after a period. It attaches to a noun with の, or to the plain form of a verb or adjective (若かったころ).
Use 三時ごろ to say roughly when to meet, and 子どものころ to recall the past. ごろ does not go with a length of time (such as 〜時間).
ぐらい／くらい is for amounts and lengths of time, while ごろ is for points in time (三時ごろ, but 三時間ぐらい). ～のころ often refers to a habit or state that continued during that period.

examples.ja: 子（こ）どもの頃（ころ）、よくここで遊（あそ）びました。
examples.romaji: Kodomo no koro, yoku koko de asobimashita.
examples.tr: When I was a child, I often played here.

examples.ja: 高校（こうこう）の頃（ころ）、毎日（まいにち）走（はし）っていた。
examples.romaji: Kōkō no koro, mainichi hashitte ita.
examples.tr: When I was in high school, I ran every day.

examples.ja: 三時（さんじ）頃（ごろ）に駅（えき）で会（あ）いましょう。
examples.romaji: Sanji goro ni eki de aimashō.
examples.tr: Let's meet at the station around three o'clock.
examples.note: After a clock time, 頃 is read ごろ.

pitfalls: Mind the reading: ごろ after clock times and dates, ころ after a period.
三時間ごろ is wrong. For a length of time, say 三時間ぐらい.
